key_insight: A two-qubit, fully parameterized quantum neural network can exhibit grokking and epoch-wise double descent, where test error first worsens and later recovers into strong generalization.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning system design, the result shows that circuit depth, learning rate, and weight decay can strongly control whether an overparameterized quantum model ultimately generalizes or destabilizes.
method: Train a 2-qubit QNN with a complete SU(4) parameterization.
Sweep circuit depth and optimization hyperparameters to track grokking onset and test-error dynamics.
Add weak explicit weight-norm regularization to stabilize late-stage training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical observations of grokking, epoch-wise double descent, and late-stage test-error decay across overparameterized quantum circuits, with regularization preserving generalization gains.
watch_item: The reported behavior is demonstrated on a small two-qubit setup, so scaling effects and hardware noise may change the stability of the proposed regularization strategy.
paper_title: Grokking and epoch-wise double descent in quantum neural networks
